The voices came first.

Photographs, familiar call signs, and the story of a website built to bring people together.

RECOVERED FROM WAYBACK

A little of the old site,
a lot of familiar faces.

The original website put a face to the voice, shared pictures of gatherings, and helped visitors find the evening net. Its pages are preserved here as a record of the community.

Pages from the past

May 2014

A welcoming home on the web

The earliest homepage capture lists three rotating operators, Rimlink repeaters, a chat room, audio streaming, member photos and Sunday coffee gatherings in Tempe. The page credits “Daddy Cool” and says it was updated April 1, 2014.

June 2014

Putting a face to the voice

The gallery pairs call signs with member photographs. The history page discusses an old 1AW QSL card and the beginnings of ARRL, with its ARRL account attributed to Wikipedia.

September–December 2018

A fuller record of the net

The later site adds a net-control script, volunteer guidance and a gallery of social gatherings. The homepage’s operator rotation has changed and several days are marked open.

About this recovery

Wayback’s calendar showed 25 homepage captures from May 2014 to September 2026, and 448 captured URLs under this prefix.

The December 26, 2018 homepage is the most useful of the homepage versions inspected. September 2018 subpages and the June 2014 gallery supplement it. The newest homepage capture redirects away from the net.

Some images were missing. No old chat or audio service has been reactivated. The archive is a historical record, not a current operating directory.

What was recovered and changed ↗
Beyond the repeater

From hamfests to Field Day.

The 2018 social page records coffee mornings in Tempe, a July 2014 Payson gathering, Arizona hamfests, station projects and Field Day at the Arizona Science Center in June 2015. These are past events, not upcoming invitations.
